Resolves #20344

Related: #20328

Collapses `.github/workflows/review-admission-mergeability.yml` from a two-stage `discover` + per-PR `publish` matrix (`1 + N_open_PRs` Ubuntu runner VMs on every `dev` merge; `2` sequential VMs on every `pull_request_target` event) into a single `jobs.publish` job that evaluates `[eventPr]` on `pull_request_target` or paginates and evaluates open `dev` PRs in-process with bounded concurrency (`MERGEABILITY_CONCURRENCY: '4'`) and `retries: 3` on `actions/github-script@v9`. Restores dedicated unit test coverage in `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/ReviewAdmissionMergeability.spec.mjs`.

Evidence: L2 (Playwright unit suite executing the committed workflow script across single-PR, multi-PR board concurrency, >32 overflow, and error/closed-PR branches + `check-workflow-concurrency.mjs`) → L2 required (all 4 close-target ACs are workflow topology, retry config, concurrency guard, and unit spec assertions).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/ReviewAdmissionMergeability.spec.mjs` (`runs in a single job without matrix VM fan-out and configures retries: 3 on actions/github-script` + `pull_request_target evaluates only its event PR; board triggers enumerate and evaluate all open dev PRs in one job`) |
| AC-2 | `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/ReviewAdmissionMergeability.spec.mjs` (`expect(step.with.retries).toBe(3)`) |
| AC-3 | `node node_modules/neo-agent-skills/scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.mjs` (`21 cancelling block(s) of 24 across 36 workflow file(s), all rerun-safe.`) |
| AC-4 | `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/ReviewAdmissionMergeability.spec.mjs` (`7 passed (458ms)` under `npm run test-unit`) |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. `agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline check-workflow-concurrency, check-guard-ci-parity, and husky pre-commit guards ran`.

## Test Evidence
All coverage runs in CI.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: the race RA-1 closes runs in this order:
  1. A `synchronize` run E (group `pr-N`) verifies head H against base B1 as mergeable.
  2. A `dev` merge moves the base to B2 and starts board sweep S (group `board`).
  3. S verifies (H, B2) as conflicting and writes `failure` to H.
  4. E's `success` lands afterwards and stays on H until the next event.

  `retries: 3` widens the window, because a retried POST can land seconds later. On `dev`, both jobs share `review-admission-mergeability-<N>`, so S would start only after E finished, and then read live state.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [ ] PR description: framing matches what the diff substantiates (no overshoot)

**Findings:** Drift, two items, both under Required Actions.
- The workflow comment above `group:` ("the newest retained run always reads live state and writes AFTER the older terminal call") now holds only within one trigger family. That is RA-1.
- #20344's Architectural Reality says the `dev` ruleset requires `review-admission/mergeability`. It doesn't: RA-2.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: A GitHub concurrency group orders runs only within one key. Splitting a key by trigger splits the ordering guarantee as well.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: The spec harness runs one controller at a time, so it cannot express an interleaving between two runs. RA-1's arm has to stage the second writer through the read stream.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A job-per-target matrix gets per-target serialization from the platform for free. Folding it into one process means building that fence in-process.
